news_drafts.headline: Aberdeenshire reports 67 vacant surplus former operational assets against a portfolio of 549
news_drafts.lead:
Aberdeenshire Council had 67 vacant surplus former operational assets at the first quarter of 2026/27, according to the Business Services performance report for the Business Services Committee. Its operational portfolio, the buildings and sites it still uses, stands at 549 at the second quarter.

The paper says the number of vacant assets is expected to fall in 2026/27 and 2027/28. A number of closures are planned for early 2027, linked to a new depot and office facility at One Harlaw Road, Inverurie. The performance target for capital receipts, the money from selling assets, is 100% of the amount budgeted.

The committee also has the Business Services budget risk register for 2026/27. It identifies a pressure on income from licensing fees and charges. In the register's words, "Pressure has been identified within Licensing fees and charges however this is currently being offset with underspends across the wider Business Services budget." The risk score for council tax and fees-and-charges collection remains at 16, unchanged, with a residual score of 12.

news_drafts.headline: Aberdeenshire's climate emissions cuts fall 69% as LED streetlighting plan loses funding
news_drafts.lead: Aberdeenshire's Environment and Infrastructure Services Committee has scaled back its planned carbon reductions for 2026/27 from 81 tonnes to 25 tonnes of CO2 equivalent, after capital funding for LED streetlighting was not allocated. In its Carbon Budget progress update, the council identified the streetlighting rollout as the main project now unable to proceed. The committee acknowledged that meeting its climate change targets requires "significant capital investment" for which long-term funding has not yet been secured. Budget pressures, the council stated, can only be managed if additional funding becomes available to support the capital spending needed for those targets.

news_drafts.headline: Aberdeenshire IJB returns to surplus but remains dependent on partner funding
news_drafts.lead: The Aberdeenshire Integration Joint Board has closed a year-end surplus and created a small general fund reserve for the first time in the accounts to 31 March 2026, marking a marked improvement on the previous year through recovery activity, partner support and strengthened financial controls. The committee noted this was the beginning of a longer-term improvement rather than a final position. Officers confirmed that reserves available in the current financial year remained limited and the IJB continued to rely on partner funding to deliver a balanced budget while savings plans were implemented. External audit has identified medium-term financial sustainability as a key focus, reflecting structural challenges including demand pressures, workforce capacity constraints and the need for service redesign. The chief internal auditor provided the most positive opinion available under internal audit standards, confirming the IJB maintained an adequate and effective framework for governance, risk management and control during the year.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 2 - Infrastructure Services Budget Risk Register 2026/27
findings.headline: A new tactical risk for Public Local Inquiries, scored 4 x 4 with residual risk 12, was added after budget setting.
findings.detail: Public Local Inquiries are planning cases examined by a Scottish Government reporter, and the register now carries them as a tactical risk. The control is monitoring of upcoming inquiries and their likely cost, and the register notes that the pipeline of inquiries and associated cost exposure will continue to be monitored.
findings.matters: A council whose planning inquiry costs were not in its budget can show that the exposure was added mid-year, which other councils may face through the same planning process.
findings.quote: New EIS tactical risk included since budget setting for Public Local Inquiries. The current assessment remains 4 x 4 with residual risk 12.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 2 - Infrastructure Services Budget Risk Register 2026/27
findings.headline: Climate-related emergency response and adaptation costs carry the register's highest score, 20, with residual risk 15, unchanged from the previous report.
findings.detail: The register records no change to this risk. It says that climate-related costs for roads, drainage, bridges, coastal defences, buildings and response could exceed budget assumptions, and it ties the risk to existing flood contingency budgets and capital programmes for roads, bridges and flood prevention.
findings.matters: A finance director can compare this council's top-scored infrastructure risk, and the controls it relies on, with the climate adaptation pressures they are carrying.
findings.quote: Climate‑related emergency response and adaptation costs remain a high exposure, with score 20 and residual risk 15.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 2 - Infrastructure Services Budget Risk Register 2026/27
findings.headline: Scotland's Route Map has moved the Circular Economy Act into implementation, with 11 priority actions, while its impact assessment says several costs remain indicative.
findings.detail: The register keeps the Circular Economy Act risk unchanged at a score of 16 with residual risk 12. It notes that the national impact assessment treats several costs as indicative and needing further policy-specific assessment.
findings.matters: A council planning for new waste duties and their costs can see that the national cost basis is still provisional, which affects how firmly any allowance in its medium-term plan can be set.
findings.figures: Risk score 16 (4 x 4); residual risk 12; 11 priority actions
findings.quote: Scotland’s Route Map has moved the Act into implementation through 11 priority actions, although its impact assessment says several costs remain indicative and require further policy-specific assessment.

findings.paper_title: Appendix 2 - Infrastructure Services Budget Risk Register 2026/27
findings.headline: The UK ETS Authority confirmed in August 2026 that waste-incineration inclusion in the Emissions Trading Scheme will not commence in 2028, with no new timetable yet announced.
findings.detail: The register previously carried a new ETS risk scored 4 x 4 with residual risk 12, on the basis of a tax on residual waste going to Energy from Waste plants from 2028. The update records the postponement and states that monitoring, reporting and verification began on 1 January 2026.
findings.matters: A finance director budgeting for a 2028 carbon cost on residual waste sent to EfW now has that start date removed, and a replacement timetable is still to come.
findings.figures: Risk score 16 (4 x 4); residual risk 12; monitoring, reporting and verification began 1 January 2026; waste-incineration inclusion was due 2028
findings.quote: The UK ETS Authority confirmed in August 2026 that waste-incineration inclusion will not commence in 2028. A new timetable is still to be announced

findings.paper_title: Market Position Statement for Older People's Care Homes and Very Sheltered Housing
findings.headline: The AHSCP acknowledges significant operational and financial risks in its provider of last resort role, which it will address through a procedure due in the last quarter of 2026-27.
findings.detail: When a provider cannot continue, the AHSCP may have to arrange alternative provision or deliver care directly. The report says past interventions carried these risks, particularly at short notice, and that a policy and procedure will go to the IJB in the last quarter of 2026-27.
findings.matters: Short-notice provider failure can require a council to take on care and its costs at once, so a reader comparing how councils plan for it would want the policy timeline.
findings.figures: The paper gives no figure. The deadline is the last quarter of 2026-27.
findings.quote: but they also carry significant operational and financial risks, particularly at short notice

daily_post.headline: Business Services Committee reserves are forecast at £1,726k at 31 March 2027, down from £2,634k at 30 September 2026
daily_post.lead: A committee's reserves falling over the year shows how much one-off funding is being used to meet pressures, which other councils would compare with their own reserve trends.
